review_notes:
I read all of Mathlib/Order/Interval/Set/SuccPred.lean (lines 1–176). I compared it with Mathlib/Order/SuccPred/Basic.lean and with the Finset and Algebra copies of the same lemmas.

The file has no @[simp] attributes. The simp-normal forms for these rewrites already exist in Basic.lean as simp lemmas under NoMaxOrder: `Ici_succ`, `Iio_succ`, `Icc_succ_left`, `Ico_succ_left`, `Ico_succ_right`, `Ioo_succ_right` and their `pred` duals. They rewrite in the same direction as this file's `*_eq_*` lemmas. Adding simp to the copies here would create competing duplicate rules, and leaving them as they are causes no simp conflict. The `_of_not_isMax` variants carry hypotheses and are correctly not simp.

I found no rewrite cycles. The insert lemmas have several equal-looking left-hand sides and are not obvious normal forms, so they are not good simp candidates. `Icc_succ_pred_eq_Ioo` holds without NoMaxOrder or NoMinOrder. With those two instances, simp already reaches `Ioo a b` through `Icc_succ_left` and the dual `Ioc_pred_right`. A simp attribute there would add little.

The duplication between this file and Basic.lean is a redundancy question, not a simp-interface defect, so I did not report it under this rubric. I did not run Lean, so I have not tested how simp behaves on these terms.
